{"id": "25349728-d9ac-4e99-b3e6-1c8c8491c1c6", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You can't get out of this commitment early. You can limit further cost and get some value from the capacity until it ends.

**Why you're stuck until the term ends**
- AWS docs say you can't delete a Provisioned Throughput by Model Units with a commitment before the term is complete.
- Your term runs to 2027-03-15, which is about 112 days from today (2026-11-23).
- Billing is hourly and doesn't depend on usage. The 6 invocations over 14 days don't change the charge. Days with no datapoints just mean no invocations that day.

**Options**

1. **Stop it renewing.** Do this first, because the docs say Provisioned Throughput auto-renews at the end of each term with the same configuration. A missed renewal would commit you to another six months.
   - Check the auto-renew setting on `claude-launch-pt` in your `get-provisioned-model-throughput` output.
   - You can turn auto-renew off with `UpdateProvisionedModelThroughput` and `disableAutoRenew=true`. The docs describe this for token-based Provisioned Throughput, and your resource is Model Units. I couldn't confirm it works for Model Units.
   - Auto-renew can't be re-enabled afterward, and the docs say the resource can't be modified for the rest of the term.
   - If the API rejects it, ask AWS Support to confirm the term ends on 2027-03-15. Set a calendar reminder for early March either way.

2. **Use the capacity you're paying for.** The money is spent whichever way you go, so extra traffic through the provisioned ARN costs nothing more.
   - Run the launch load tests and evaluations through it now.
   - Send internal tools, dev/test traffic, batch jobs and offline evals to the provisioned model ARN.
   - You can also use it to warm up the launch path, so launch day is already validated.
